To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transient and steady-state performance are determined by a set of parameters that includes the noncircularity of the signal, the filter order, and the step size.

the transient performance of the QLMS filters is determined by the augmented statistics of the input, while the steady-state performance is determined by the second-order augmented statistics of the filter input.

the performance of a QLMS filter in a nonstationary correlated Gaussian environment is governed by the complete second-order augmented statistics of the input quaternion signal, and that the widely linear QLNS filter outperforms the semiwidely and strictly linear QLNS filters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance of adaptive filters in a nonstationary context and the development of a theoretical analysis of quaternion adaptive filters.

the analysis of adaptive filters in the quaternion domain, which has been largely unexplored, and the results presented in this work can be used as a basis for the design of optimal adaptive filters for quaternion-valued signals.
the development of a general framework for analyzing the mean and mean-square performance of adaptive filters with quaternion-valued weights in nonstationary scenarios.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the widely linear QLNS filter is always superior to the other two classes of QLNS filters.
the QLMS filter with Gaussian inputs is a semiwidely linear filter.

, in the presence of nonstationary environments, the widely linear QLNS filter exhibits the best transient and steady-state performance, followed by the semiwidely linear filter, while the linear filter exhibits the worst performance, which can be explained by the fact that the widely linear filter is able to exploit more information about the input signal than the other two filters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide a complete analysis framework for the transient and steady-state performance evaluation of quaternion adaptive filters, including the widely linear QLMSN filter, in nonstationary Gaussian environments, which has not been reported in the literature.
the proposed framework provides a complete and rigorous performance analysis of quaternion adaptive filters in the context of nonstationary environments.
the proposed framework allows us to obtain closed-form expressions for performance of quaternion adaptive filters in terms of their augmented statistics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the QLMS filter performance is not affected by the input signal noncircularity, but it is affected by the input nonstationarity.
the QLMS filter with correlated Gaussian inputs has the fastest convergence rate among all the three classes of the QLMS filters.
the performance of a widely linear adaptive filter is better than the performance of the strictly linear and semiwidely linear adaptive filters in noncircular non-Gaussian environments.
